plan.topic: Pneumonic plague incubation period: why contact observation ends after about a week
plan.angle: Title: 'Pneumonic Plague Incubation: How Fast Symptoms Can Start (CDC and WHO) #shorts'. Answer within 10 s: CDC says pneumonic plague symptoms can start as soon as 1 day after exposure, and WHO says plague symptoms usually appear within 1 to 7 days. That's why health authorities monitor close contacts and give them a 7-day course of preventive antibiotics (WHO). Status, credited and dated: as of Oct 8, 2026, the Irkutsk oblast governor said quarantine had been lifted; WHO says it has asked for more information; plague is not confirmed and not ruled out. Close: a possible exposure plus fever, cough, shortness of breath or chest pain means contact a doctor or local health authority urgently. 'If you're worried, talk to a health professional.' Point viewers to L1.
plan.working_title: Pneumonic Plague Incubation: Why Contacts Are Watched for About a Week #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1 that drives viewers to the long video. 'Plague incubation period' is a plain search question with low competition, timed to the quarantine news. | fact-check: The angle depends on a CDC 'window' that would justify ending observation after about a week. CDC's page doesn't give one: it only says pneumonic incubation 'can be as short as 1 day'. Neither CDC nor WHO says observation ends after about a week. WHO gives 1–7 days for Y. pestis in general and recommends 7-day chemoprophylaxis for close contacts. Don't say or imply that Irkutsk stood down because of the incubation period; that is our inference. Keep the status line dated and attributed, and list CDC's 4 pneumonic warning signs in full.

package.description:
Pneumonic plague incubation can be as short as 1 day (CDC). WHO says plague symptoms often appear after 1 to 7 days, and advises monitoring close contacts of pneumonic plague patients and giving them 7 days of preventive antibiotics. Status as of Oct 8, 2026: not confirmed, not ruled out in the Irkutsk oblast case. WHO's chief asked Russia to clarify reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause; Russia's health regulator said no infections were found among staff.
Possible exposure plus fever, cough, shortness of breath or chest pain? Contact a doctor or local health authority urgently. Never self-treat.
#PublicHealth #PlagueFacts #HealthScience #InfectiousDisease

script.working_title: Pneumonic Plague Incubation: How Fast Symptoms Can Start (CDC and WHO) #shorts
script.hook_pattern: A plain search question answered right away with an agency number ('How fast can pneumonic plague start?', then CDC: as short as 1 day). Next comes WHO's 1–7 day range, then a dated news status that credits each line to the body that said it and gives both sides of the Oct 8 development. It ends on WHO's 7-day preventive antibiotics for contacts, CDC's curable-with-quick-treatment line and an urgent-care close.

factcheck.summary: I checked every factual claim against its cited source and all 7 sources are real and reachable. The incubation lines match their sources. CDC says pneumonic plague "can be as short as 1 day" (page last reviewed May 15, 2024). WHO says people often develop symptoms "after an incubation period of one to seven days" (fact sheet dated Sep 29, 2026). WHO's guidance to identify and monitor close contacts and give them 7 days of preventive antibiotics is correct. CDC's line "Plague can be cured with antibiotics, but treatment must be given quickly" matches (About Plague, last reviewed Aug 24, 2026), and so do CDC's 4 pneumonic warning signs. The Oct 8 news lines are correctly credited and dated. Kyiv Independent says Russian state media reported the quarantine lifted. Russian authorities call the death "pneumonia of unknown etiology". Al Jazeera reports Tedros asked Russia to clarify "media reports of a second employee with pneumonia of undetermined cause", and that Rospotrebnadzor said there were "no infections detected among staff". PBS/AP backs up both sides. I searched for anything newer than Oct 8 and found nothing that changes the status. The safety lines are all there: urgent contact, never self-treat, and the worried line. The script is about 169 words, inside the 170 guide. There are 3 small fixes: date the closing status line, remove a cited source that no line uses, and optionally tighten the CDC scope in s1.

notes: At 12.9s a 'Y. pestis' label sits directly behind/under the caption pill, showing as a clipped 'Y.p' fragment overlapping the '1 TO 7 DAYS.' caption — matches the automated overlap finding at t=12.91.

Caption spells the date phonetically as 'ON OCTOBER EIGHTH,' instead of numerals, breaking the 'dates as numerals' rule and making it inconsistent with the pill above it which correctly reads 'As of Oct 8, 2026'.
Caption ends on a trailing comma, leaving a hanging fragment.

Automated audit flags a 'Pneumonia' label overlapping the caption text at both 27.0s and 34.9s ('the death as pneumonia' / 'employee with pneumonia'); the label is not cleanly separated from the caption band in either sampled frame.
Good catch: the status card correctly keeps 'Not confirmed. Not ruled out.' together on one screen with the dated sub-line.
But the caption pill 'AND IT'S NOT' ends on the word 'not', an incomplete hanging fragment that risks reading as a standalone (and wrong) claim if the next caption is delayed or missed.

Both captions in this shot end on a trailing comma ('OF PNEUMONIC PLAGUE PATIENTS,' and 'WHO SAYS TO IDENTIFY THEM,'), which the caption rules explicitly forbid and makes each screen read as an unfinished sentence.

A ghost 'Antibiotic' label is visible peeking out from under the caption pill at the bottom-left in both sampled frames, overlapping 'Here's the good news:' and 'when they're given quickly.' per the automated findings at 58.87s and 63.91s.
Caption 'HAD A POSSIBLE EXPOSURE,' ends on a trailing comma, an incomplete-looking fragment on screen even though the next caption continues the sentence.
Caption at 73.1s reads 'OR LOCAL HEALTH' — a bare, dangling fragment (this is the exact kind of fragment called out as a hard rule violation elsewhere in QA notes).
Caption 'THERE'S MORE ON THE' ends on the orphaned word 'THE', a dangling fragment with no clear meaning on its own screen.

Final frame (82.0s) is visually sparse — just a heart mascot, a small phone icon and a tiny floating doctor icon on a plain gradient with no headline/caption, which risks reading as empty dead space on an outro beat.

audio.soundNotes: Music under voice (−13.5 dB) already sits in the target window, so gain stays at 1.0; pause level (−9.6 dB) is a touch hot but only occurs in ~11% of runtime and is driven by natural lack of ducking, not an overall level problem. Thinned several redundant simultaneous swoosh/whoosh/tick doublets (i13, i23, i34, i46, i50, i54, i59) that were stacking on top of a pop/swoosh at the same instant, especially around the busy 72–78 s stretch and the final two transitions, so no beat exceeds 3 effects. Nudged the "Not confirmed. Not ruled out." hit (i20) and the "7 days (WHO)" swell (i27) up slightly to give those two reveals a touch more presence while staying under the voice. Added restrained custom cues at the key reveal, the reassurance beat, the urgency call, and the closing line to carry emotion without adding clutter.
